research: Darkhorse Analytics' well-known "Data Looks Better Naked" animated GIF, a widely used data-visualization teaching resource

images.note: Real static frame extracted (via ffmpeg, no AI alteration) from Darkhorse Analytics' published 'Data Looks Better Naked' animated GIF — the 'before' state: a bar chart with a wood-grain background, gray plot area, gridlines, a redundant color legend, and heavy borders.

Real static final frame from the same GIF — the 'after' state, once every step of removal (background, legend, gridlines, bolding, borders) has been applied and only the single most important bar is highlighted in color.

imageNote: This lesson is conceptual (data-viz design principles), not Tableau-GUI-specific, so per instructions a broad web search was used instead of help.tableau.com. Darkhorse Analytics' 'Data Looks Better Naked' is a real, widely cited before/after data-ink-ratio demonstration (not authored by LTV or AI-generated) — its animated GIF was downloaded and two genuine frames (an early one, before any cleanup, and the final one, after every cleanup step) were extracted with ffmpeg to use as static before/after screenshots, since the slide renderer needs static images. No image was invented, redrawn, or AI-cleaned; both frames are pixel-for-pixel as published by Darkhorse Analytics, with attribution given in guide.md.
